def: A bug where untrusted input changes the meaning of a SQL query (input becomes executable SQL).
A query where SQL structure and user-provided values are sent separately, preventing values from becoming syntax.
Giving a user/service only the permissions it needs; limits damage if something goes wrong.
A one-way function mapping input to a fixed-size output; small input changes produce very different outputs.
Storing a one-way derived value (not the plaintext password) so you can verify logins by hashing again and comparing.
Random per-password data mixed into hashing so identical passwords don’t produce identical hashes.
A tunable setting that makes password hashing intentionally slower to increase the cost of guessing attacks.
A password hashing algorithm designed to be slow and salted, with a configurable cost parameter.
A fast general-purpose hash that is not safe for password storage and is broken for collision resistance.
Two different inputs that produce the same hash output (a property attackers can exploit in some contexts).
A bug where attackers get script to run in a victim’s browser by injecting content into a page.
An XSS variant caused by client-side JavaScript writing untrusted data into the DOM in an unsafe way.
